content.text:
# Requirements

## 1. Automatic break after a focus session

P1 · MVP
Source: the work ("Add short and long breaks after focus sessions"), intake answer 1 (automatic), product.md (`focus start`)

As a person using the Pomodoro method, I want a break to start by itself when my focus session ends, so that I rest without running another command.

- 1.1 WHEN a focus session started with `focus start` ends, THE APP SHALL save the focus session and then start a break countdown in the same run, without further input.
- 1.2 WHEN a break starts and no long break is due (see story 2), THE APP SHALL run a short break of 5 minutes.
- 1.3 WHEN a break starts, THE APP SHALL print one line naming the break kind and its length, for example "Done. Short break: 5 minutes."
- 1.4 WHEN a break ends, THE APP SHALL save it as a session with its kind (`shortBreak` or `longBreak`), start time and end time, print "Break over.", and exit.
- 1.5 IF the run is interrupted during a break, THEN THE APP SHALL keep the already saved focus session and save no session for the break.
- 1.6 IF the run is interrupted during a focus session, THEN THE APP SHALL save no session and start no break.

> [!ASSUMPTION]
> Break lengths are fixed in this version: 5 minutes for a short break and 15 minutes for a long break, as in the standard Pomodoro method. They cannot be changed by the user.

> [!ASSUMPTION]
> After a break ends the app exits. The next focus session starts only when the user runs `focus start` again; the app does not loop.

> [!ASSUMPTION]
> Breaks are saved in the same day file as focus sessions, using the existing `shortBreak` and `longBreak` kinds. Only breaks that run to the end are saved.

## 2. Long break after every 4th focus session

P1 · MVP
Source: feedback.txt ("After 4 focus sessions I want a longer break"), intake answer 1 (counted per day, every 4th focus session)

As a person using the Pomodoro method, I want a longer break after every 4th focus session of the day, so that I recover properly after a full round.

- 2.1 WHEN a focus session ends and the number of focus sessions saved for that day, including the one just ended, is a multiple of 4, THE APP SHALL run a long break of 15 minutes instead of a short break.
- 2.2 WHEN a focus session ends and that number is not a multiple of 4, THE APP SHALL run a short break.
- 2.3 THE APP SHALL count only sessions of kind `focus` towards the long break; saved breaks do not change the count.
- 2.4 WHEN the first focus session of a new day ends, THE APP SHALL count from 1, whatever the count was on the day before.
- 2.5 WHEN a long break starts, THE APP SHALL print "Done. Long break: 15 minutes."

> [!ASSUMPTION]
> The long break is decided from the sessions saved on disk for the day, not from memory in the running process. Closing the terminal between sessions does not reset the count.

> [!ASSUMPTION]
> A session belongs to the day of its start time, the same day `Store` uses to choose the `yyyy-MM-dd.json` file. The count for the long break and the goal progress both use this day.

## 3. Goal progress in `focus log`

P1 · MVP
Source: the work ("a daily goal … that `focus log` shows progress against"), feedback.txt ("A goal like 8 sessions a day would help")

As a person who never knows when to stop, I want `focus log` to show how many focus sessions I have done today against my daily goal, so that I know when I am finished for the day.

- 3.1 WHEN the user runs `focus log`, THE APP SHALL list today's saved sessions in start order, one per line, showing each one's kind (`focus`, `shortBreak` or `longBreak`) and start time.
- 3.2 WHEN the user runs `focus log`, THE APP SHALL print a last line with today's progress in the form "Goal: 3/8 focus sessions", where the first number is today's saved focus sessions and the second is the daily goal.
- 3.3 WHEN today's focus sessions equal or exceed the daily goal, THE APP SHALL add " — goal reached" to the progress line and show the real count, for example "Goal: 9/8 focus sessions — goal reached".
- 3.4 WHEN no daily goal has been set, THE APP SHALL use a goal of 8 focus sessions.
- 3.5 WHEN today has no saved sessions, THE APP SHALL print only the progress line, with a count of 0.
- 3.6 THE APP SHALL count only sessions of kind `focus` towards the goal.

> [!ASSUMPTION]
> Breaks are shown in `focus log` as their own lines, in the same format as focus sessions. Goal progress is one plain text line at the end, without a progress bar or colours.

> [!ASSUMPTION]
> The default daily goal is 8 focus sessions, the number named in the user feedback.

<!-- MVP line -->

## 4. Set the daily goal

P2
Source: intake answer 2 (you decide), feedback.txt (daily goal), principles.md (local files only)

As a person with my own working rhythm, I want to set my daily goal, so that progress is measured against a number that fits me.

- 4.1 WHEN the user runs `focus goal <n>` with a whole number from 1 to 99, THE APP SHALL save that number as the daily goal and print "Daily goal: <n> focus sessions".
- 4.2 WHEN the user runs `focus goal` without a number, THE APP SHALL print the current daily goal and change nothing.
- 4.3 IF the user runs `focus goal` with a value that is not a whole number from 1 to 99, THEN THE APP SHALL print a usage message naming the allowed range and leave the saved goal unchanged.
- 4.4 WHEN a goal has been saved, THE APP SHALL use it in every later `focus log` until it is changed, on every day.
- 4.5 WHEN the user runs the app with no command or an unknown command, THE APP SHALL print a usage line that includes `goal`.

> [!ASSUMPTION]
> The daily goal is stored in a local JSON file, `settings.json`, in `~/Library/Application Support/FocusTimer/`, next to the day files. It is set with the command `focus goal <n>`; there is no flag, environment variable or hand-edited config.

> [!ASSUMPTION]
> The goal is one number for all days. Changing it also changes the progress shown for today; past days are not stored with their old goal.

## 5. Goal notice when a focus session ends

P3
Source: feedback.txt ("I never know when to stop")

As a person in the middle of a working day, I want to see my progress when a focus session ends, so that I know where I stand without running `focus log`.

- 5.1 WHEN a focus session ends, THE APP SHALL print today's progress line in the same form as `focus log`, before the break line.
- 5.2 WHEN the focus session that just ended makes today's count equal to the daily goal, THE APP SHALL print "Daily goal reached." once, for that session only.

> [!ASSUMPTION]
> Milestones: milestone 1 is the MVP, stories 1 to 3 (automatic breaks, long break, progress in `focus log` against the default goal of 8). Milestone 2 is story 4 (set the goal). Milestone 3 is story 5 (goal notice after a session). Each milestone can ship alone.

## Quality requirements

Source: Intake (privacy, speed, offline), principles.md, tech.md

- Q1 THE APP SHALL do everything in this spec without network access and without an account.
- Q2 THE APP SHALL keep sessions and the daily goal only in local files under `~/Library/Application Support/FocusTimer/` and send no data anywhere.
- Q3 WHEN the user runs `focus log` or `focus goal` on a day with up to 100 saved sessions, THE APP SHALL finish its output in under 1 second.
- Q4 WHEN a focus session ends, THE APP SHALL start the break countdown within 2 seconds.
- Q5 WHEN the app writes a day file or the settings file, THE APP SHALL write it atomically, so an interrupted write leaves the earlier file intact.
- Q6 THE APP SHALL read day files written before this feature (focus sessions only) without conversion, and keep the day file format readable by the existing `Session` model.
- Q7 THE APP SHALL decide the break kind and the goal progress from values passed in (the saved sessions, the goal and the current time), so that both can be tested with fixed dates and no real clock or waiting.
- Q8 THE APP SHALL use only Foundation and the Swift standard library for this feature.

## Edge cases

- Story 1: the user presses Ctrl-C during the break. The focus session stays saved, the break is not saved, and the next `focus start` begins a new focus session.
- Story 1: the focus session cannot be saved (for example the folder is not writable). The app reports the error, exits with a non-zero status and starts no break.
- Story 1: a focus session ends just before midnight and the break starts after it. The break is saved in the next day's file, by its own start time; the focus session stays in the day it started.
- Story 2: the 4th focus session is interrupted. It is not saved, so the count stays at 3 and the next finished focus session is the 4th and gets the long break.
- Story 2: the user interrupts the long break after the 4th session. The 5th focus session is followed by a short break; the missed long break is not made up.
- Story 2: the 8th and 12th focus sessions of a day also get a long break, as each is a multiple of 4.
- Story 2: three focus sessions were done yesterday and none today. Today's first focus session is followed by a short break.
- Story 2: the day file exists but cannot be decoded. The app reports the error and does not overwrite the file; no break kind is guessed.
- Story 3: today's file is missing. `focus log` prints "Goal: 0/8 focus sessions" and no session lines.
- Story 3: today has only breaks saved (a break that started after midnight). The breaks are listed and the progress count is 0.
- Story 3: `settings.json` is missing or cannot be decoded. `focus log` uses the default goal of 8 and does not change the file.
- Story 3: the user did more focus sessions than the goal. The line shows the real count, for example "Goal: 10/8 focus sessions — goal reached".
- Story 4: the user runs `focus goal 0`, `focus goal -3`, `focus goal 2.5` or `focus goal many`. The usage message is printed and the saved goal stays as it was.
- Story 4: the goal is lowered below today's count. `focus log` shows the goal as reached straight away.
